item.content:encoded:
Nigeria Election Security Tracker October 2026Centre for Democracy & Development (CDD-West Africa)

发布源: Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

CDD-West Africa’s October 2026 Election Security Tracker examines emerging threats to Nigeria’s 2027 elections, documenting election-related violence, broader insecurity, misinformation and hate speech. The report highlights a 22.07% decline in recorded security incidents alongside a 61.62% rise in reported deaths, with election-related incidents also increasing. It assesses regional security trends, implications for political participation and electoral preparations, and priority actions to strengthen election security and resilience.

item.content:encoded:
Community Resistance and Reintegration Gaps in Nigeria's Operation Safe Corridor ProgrammeDr. Oge Samuel Okonkwo

发布源: Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

More than 300,000 people linked to Boko Haram and its ISWAP faction surrendered or exited the bush between 2016 and 2025, according toBorno State security officials. Not everyone in this total passed through the federal government's Operation Safe Corridor (OSC). Many surrendered through Borno State's own Borno Model, a parallel track running lighter screening and processing far larger numbers, according toa separate assessment by International Crisis Group. Only 3,442 completed OSC itself, the federal government's flagship deradicalization, rehabilitation and reintegration programme, according tothe Armed Forces of Nigeria. A recent batch of 744 graduated in early 2026. Defence Headquarters celebrated the batch as proof of a national resolve to fix the human dimensions of the conflict. These are two different measures. The Borno Model shows large numbers of fighters leaving the bush once offered amnesty. OSC shows how few of them the federal government formally processes back into society. Defection is not Nigeria's bottleneck. Reintegration is, and the distance between these tracks is where policy attention belongs.

Nigeria launched OSC in 2016 after years of purely military operations failed to end the insurgency in the Northeast, according toInternational Crisis Group. The programme runs a structured cycle at a facility in Gombe State. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Operation Safe Corridor and the Path to Sustainable Reintegration: A SWOT Assessment of Rehabilitation and Reintegration in NigeriaCentre for Democracy & Development (CDD-West Africa)

发布源: Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

The assessment identifies three principal strengths: an institutionalised exit route, the complementary capacities of 17 government institutions, and a structured rehabilitation curriculum. Participantsparticularly valued psychological care, religious engagement and vocational training. The programme combines military coordination and protection with  specialist rehabilitation and assigns responsibility for reintegration to state governments. In May 2026, the coordinator reported that more than 3,000 participants had been reintegrated during its first decade.1 Sustained civilian life beyond the camp remains the more demanding test of its effectiveness.

The principal weaknesses stem from the uneven fulfilment of shared institutional responsibilities. Defence Headquarters carries a disproportionate operational and financial burden, supplemented by development partners. Contributions from participating agencies are insufficiently institutionalised and can depend on the commitment of individual officeholders. Funding constraints, staff shortages and weak state ownership outside Borno limit care and support after graduation. Fragmented follow up and inadequate livelihood and family assistance compound these difficulties. Limited community participation in investigations and access to court proceedings also weaken confidence in the legaldecisions preceding return. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在IMANI Center for Policy and Education --Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Centre for Energy and Climate Policy

发布源: IMANI Center for Policy and Education --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policyat IMANI is dedicated to finding lasting solutions to the persistent challenges in Ghana & Africa’s energy & climate sector. Despite numerous efforts to address the sector’s issues, progress has often fallen short due to a general lack of a comprehensive “follow through” approach. This underscores the need for remedial measures and their implementation to adopt a new direction and focus.

We believe that solving the energy & climate sector problems requires a multifaceted approach that includes thorough diagnosis of the sector’s issues, the development of innovative solutions, or the adoption of tried-and-tested remedial measures. Crucially, it also involves consistently tracking the implementation of these measures. This holistic approach informs our research and advocacy efforts at the Centre, ensuring that we contribute effectively to sustainable energy and climate policies in Ghana and across Africa.

Improving the Performance of State Actors in the Energy Sector-

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policy at IMANI Ghana assesses the performance of state actors in the energy sector. We evaluate public sector agencies responsible for energy based on key indicators such as transparency, efficiency, autonomy, and financial accountability. Through this comprehensive assessment, we aim to drive improvements and promote best practices within the sector, ensuring a sustainable and efficient energy landscape for Ghana and beyond.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
AN ANALYSIS OF THE GOVERNMENT OF GHANA’S 2026 MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW – POLICY BRIEF 26

发布源: Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) --Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-13

The mid-year budget review that was presented to Parliament on July 23, 2026, provided an opportunity for the government to report on the implementation of the 2026 budget, reassess the macroeconomic and fiscal outlooks for the year, and outline policy measures to support the realization of the government’s economic and fiscal objectives for 2026. This paper critically analyzes the review. Even though we find aspects of the review and the macroeconomic developments that are positive, we identify in this paper a number of important weaknesses about the review, which have undermined the credibility of the budget and the government’s ability to achieve its stated goals and objectives.
